title: Seattle Diwali Celebration Disrupted by Protesters Carrying 'Deport All Dot Heads' Placards
excerpt: Far-right activist Jake Lang and Thomas Allen targeted a Seattle Diwali festival where children were performing, drawing condemnation from Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal and Indian-American groups.
body:
• Far-right activist Jake Lang and fellow protester Thomas Allen tried to disrupt a Seattle Diwali celebration on Saturday, carrying placards reading "Deport All Dot Heads" and "Stop Hindu Replacement of Christians".
  • Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal, who represents Seattle, said she was "beyond disgusted" and that the community should feel safe to celebrate Diwali.
  • The Coalition of Hindus of North America urged vigilance, saying the activists have announced plans to disrupt other celebrations.
  • For diaspora families attending remaining Diwali events in the Seattle area, community groups advise staying alert and reporting hate incidents to police and organisers.

A Diwali celebration in Seattle was disrupted on Saturday after far-right activist Jake Lang and fellow protester Thomas Allen arrived carrying placards reading "Deport All Dot Heads" and "Stop Hindu Replacement of Christians", according to ANI reporting of the incident. Video from the scene showed the two men holding signs targeting Hindus before they were physically stopped and removed by people at the event, at a family celebration where children were performing.

Lang later posted on X claiming he and other protesters had been assaulted by attendees, and posted abusive remarks targeting the Hindu community. In one post quoted by ANI, he said they "didn't like our 'Deport All Dot Heads' sign" and blamed Hindus for flipping Texas blue for the Democrats. Speaking outside the venue, he said they were demonstrating their First Amendment rights against what he called the replacement of Christians by Hindus in Texas and Washington, and claimed they were hit and his flag was broken.

"I am beyond disgusted by this vile and racist display. Diwali is an important holiday and our community should feel safe to celebrate it. This hateful display has no place in our city or this country."

— Pramila Jayapal, US Congresswoman for Seattle

Condemnation from Indian-American leaders

US Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal, who represents Seattle in the House of Representatives, condemned the disruption in a post on X. Prominent Indian-American businessman Ajay Jain Bhutoria called the action "pure hate and bigotry", saying in a post quoted by ANI: "Diwali is a festival of light, family, and joy — not a threat. Targeting Hindu Americans and Indian immigrants with racial slurs and conspiracy rhetoric has no place in this country."

The Coalition of Hindus of North America (CoHNA) issued a community alert for Seattle and surrounding areas. "Hinduphobic bigotry on open display as activists Jake Lang and Thomas Allen burst in to disrupt a Hindu Diwali celebration where children are performing," CoHNA said, adding that others at the event removed them from the premises. The organisation advised community members to stay vigilant while celebrating Diwali, saying the activists have announced plans to disrupt other celebrations. Reporting on the incident is available from ANI via APNA MA TV and Jugti's diaspora coverage.

Who is Jake Lang?

According to the ANI reports, Lang runs an organisation called White Replacement and was a participant in the January 6, 2021 attack on the US Capitol, for which he served four years in jail. He was pardoned by US President Donald Trump on the first day of his second presidency in 2025.

Context for the community

The attempted disruption came in the same period as official Diwali celebrations across Washington state. Governor Bob Ferguson joined a Diwali celebration at the state's Legislative Building alongside the Consul General of India and Senator Manka Dhingra, and proclaimed Sunday to be Diwali, the Festival of Lights, in Washington state, noting that Washington is home to one of the largest Indian-American communities in the country. The incident also came just after President Trump marked Diwali at the White House, and days after a 19-year-old suspect, identified as Alexandros Paporakis, was arrested over an alleged plan to target a Hindu temple near Chicago, according to ANI.

That contrast is the point community leaders made: Diwali is being celebrated openly at the White House, at state capitols and in cities across the United States, while a public family festival in Seattle was targeted with explicit anti-Hindu slogans. No injuries or arrests at the Seattle festival were reported in the sources reviewed for this article.

What to do next

For families attending Diwali events in the Seattle area this weekend, CoHNA's advice is to stay vigilant and report disruptions. If you witness a hate incident at a public celebration, move children and vulnerable attendees away from confrontation, alert venue staff or police, and preserve video or photos to share with organisers and law enforcement rather than engaging protesters directly.
